decisions.reason: As a low-cost incremental burner component tied to the firm's installed radiant-heater base, it still has service and replacement value and there is not enough negative evidence to justify withdrawal.
As the flagship electric infrared line with several models and a strong fit to the firm's electrification strategy, its strategic upside remains high and the firm is unlikely to abandon it now.

After two years on the market, this halogen variant remains a more peripheral and overlapping electric option, so the firm would likely prune it and redeploy attention to stronger core lines and new development.

The hydrogen-capable line preserves an important decarbonization option with high potential upside, and the firm would continue to keep that option open while the market and regulatory path remain uncertain.
